verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as a content discrepancy. The claim's raw observation about indentation is factually correct, but it is a systemic page-break formatting artifact with zero text loss and no change of meaning, and two of its three stated consequences are demonstrably false.

(1) The PDF hierarchy is exactly as claimed - I measured it rather than eyeballing it. Leftmost-ink column per text line at 300dpi: page 701 (right-hand page) has outer rule markers '8)'/'9)' at x=336, outer body text at x=409, the sub-markers 'a)'/'b)' at x=408, and the body paragraphs under 9)a) at x=480. Page 702 (left-hand page, mirrored gutter, ~69px narrower left margin) has outer markers '10)'/'11)' and 'FORMAT 2' at x=267-269, outer body text at x=339, the seven disputed blocks at x=412-415, and the bodies of items 1./2./3. one level deeper at x=486-488. Step size is a consistent ~72px per level. Normalising for the 69px mirrored-margin offset, the disputed blocks land at 412 vs the 480-69=411 predicted for 9)a)-body level - a 1px match. So the PDF unambiguously places all seven blocks at the body level of 9)b), and 10) returns to the outer level. Confirmed.

(2) The markdown side is also as claimed: lines 28698-28710 are all at column 0, while page 701 preserves the convention (28684 '   a)' = 3 spaces, 28686/28688 = 6 spaces, 28690 '   b)' = 3 spaces). Confirmed.

(3) But this is not a page-702 defect - it is a document-wide page-break artifact. I checked every page anchor in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: of 1261 pages, the first content line (after skipping the page anchor, '## Page N' and the running-header line) is at indent 0 on 1261 of 1261 pages. Not one page in the entire transcription carries indentation across a page break; 67 boundaries interrupt an actively-indented context and all 67 dedent to column 0. The transcriber resets the indent to zero at every page start. This is precisely the 'page-break furniture / formatting' class the verification protocol says to reject.

(4) No text is missing, reordered, or altered. All seven blocks are present verbatim, in the correct order, immediately following '   b) If the groups are of unequal length:'. Nothing is misplaced - only leading whitespace differs - so the kind 'misplaced-content' is itself a mischaracterisation.

(5) The stated consequences do not survive scrutiny. The claim that 'the 1./2./3. procedure appears to be a free-standing rule that always applies' is refuted by the line directly above it, which is retained verbatim in the markdown: '...each location that occupies the excess part is space filled, according to the following recursive procedure:'. That colon-introduced lead-in binds items 1-3 unambiguously; they cannot read as free-standing. The claim that "'as defined in General rule 9a above' loses its anchor" is refuted by the sentence naming its own anchor explicitly - and General rule 9 a) is present and correctly labelled at line 28684. Likewise, 'unequal length' splits exactly into the retained 'longer than' and 'shorter than' paragraphs, and 9)b) would otherwise have an empty body, so the scope is recoverable from the text alone with no ambiguity a reader could act on. The implementable content of the variable-length group MOVE rule is unchanged.

Verdict: real=false - true observation, but page-break/whitespace formatting only, systemic across all 1261 pages, with complete text and no change in meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The indentation observation is accurate (PDF places the seven blocks at the 9)b) body level, x=412-415 vs outer level x=267; markdown writes them at column 0), but it is an instance of a transcription-wide convention rather than a page-702 error: the first content line of all 1261 pages in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is flush left, and none of the 67 page breaks that interrupt an indented context preserve the indent. All text is present verbatim and in the correct order, nothing is misplaced, and the scope of the material remains explicit in the retained prose ('according to the following recursive procedure:' introduces items 1-3; 'as defined in General rule 9a above' names its own anchor, which is intact at line 28684). If the project wants nesting preserved across page breaks, that is a single global transcription-normalisation task (inherit the enclosing indent level at each page start), not a per-page content finding, and it should be filed once at that level rather than ledgered page by page.
